title: The Cajun Navy: Heroes or Liability?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with tour banter (Josh's appearance on Hanging with Doctor Z and meeting Kids in the Hall alumni), then examine the Cajun Navy, the volunteer boat-rescue groups that grew out of Hurricane Katrina and became organized around 2016's Baton Rouge floods. They cover the Zello app, the "act first" credo, the Hurricane Harvey nursing home incident in Port Arthur, political reactions including Trump's praise and the Coast Guard's objections, FEMA distrust, Helene conspiracy theories, liability and vigilantism concerns, training, and charity vetting via Charity Navigator. The episode closes with listener mail thanking audiences on the recent tour and promoting upcoming dates.

segments.title: Opening banter and tour anecdotes
segments.summary: Josh describes performing on Hanging with Doctor Z and meeting Dave Foley, Scott Thompson, Bruce McCullough and Kevin McDonald at a hotel; Chuck responds and they transition to the Cajun Navy topic.

segments.title: Introduction to the Cajun Navy
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Cajun Navy as a volunteer group that formed in response to Hurricane Katrina, when residents with boats answered calls for help beyond FEMA.

segments.title: Katrina origins and rescue numbers
segments.summary: Chuck explains that competing origin stories trace back to Katrina and the federal response failure. Josh describes Nick Gautreau's call for boats, the roughly 400 volunteers who showed up, and CBS News' report of about 10,000 rescues.

segments.title: Founders and the specialized skills of Cajun boatmen
segments.summary: Josh introduces Todd Terrell, a seafood business owner who became a founder of the United Cajun Navy. Chuck describes the groups' organization and the expert boat skills of members, noting the lack of search and rescue training as a key criticism.

segments.title: 2016 Baton Rouge flood and the Zello app
segments.summary: Josh describes the 2016 Louisiana flood and the role of smartphones and social media in organizing. Chuck explains how the Zello app turns phones into walkie-talkies with translation, improving coordination.

segments.title: Cajun accent translation aside
segments.summary: A brief exchange about whether Zello translates the Cajun accent, with a reference to Doug Shashery and sausage balls.

segments.title: Cajun Navy scale and nonprofit status
segments.summary: Josh notes that the three main nonprofit groups have multimillion-dollar budgets, chapters nationwide, and volunteer staffing funded by donations. Hosts take a break before discussing the group's act-first credo.

segments.title: Act first credo and the Port Arthur nursing home incident
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Cajun Navy's act-first credo and its benefits in Hurricane Harvey. In Port Arthur, volunteers including Ben Husser evacuated a flooded nursing home after a director cited corporate policy requiring National Guard evacuation. Chuck covers the risks and the contested nature of the incident.

segments.title: Political reactions and distrust of government
segments.summary: Josh describes Trump's association with John Bridges and the Cajun Navy, along with a later critical comment about leaving rescues to professionals. Brian Trasher, a vice president of United Cajun Navy, argues that Katrina showed people cannot rely on government. The hosts discuss distrust of government and the Bush FEMA response.

segments.title: Coast Guard pushback and liability to officials
segments.summary: Amanda Faulkner, a Coast Guard spokesperson, said the Coast Guard had enough boats. Hosts discuss when volunteers become a liability and the untrained nature of volunteer evacuations versus National Guard training.

segments.title: Hurricane Helene and FEMA conspiracy theories
segments.summary: Josh describes Hurricane Helene in 2024 and the spread of rumors that FEMA would seize property. Chuck explains how social media amplified distrust and that the Cajun Navy should not disparage official efforts.

segments.title: Working with government and logistics
segments.summary: Todd Terrell says the groups try to work with government but that FEMA is not designed for the Cajun Navy's speed. Chuck notes the advantage of quickly delivering supplies.

segments.title: Critique of reliance on volunteers and need for institutions
segments.summary: Josh cites Miriam Markowitz's GQ article arguing that heroism should be systemic and funded by taxes rather than micro-donations. Chuck agrees institutions should work but notes volunteers are not reliable enough in every situation.

segments.title: Evacuation discouragement and rescue-the-rescuers concerns
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether Cajun Navy presence could discourage evacuation, and the rumor about Hurricane Michael volunteers stranded in a hotel, which Chuck says was not supported by evidence.

segments.title: Vigilantism and legal liability
segments.summary: Chuck raises vigilantism and mob rule concerns, comparing to neighborhood watch. Josh raises legal and moral liability for startup groups.

segments.title: Immunity, training, and integration with responders
segments.summary: Chuck explains government responders have civil immunity that volunteers lack, and suggests training and coordination. He notes that Cajun Navy Relief and United Cajun Navy require training. Josh expects training to become more rigorous over time.

segments.title: Charity ratings and donation advice
segments.summary: Chuck cites Charity Navigator ratings of 85 for United Cajun Navy and 87 for Cajun Navy Relief, notes leaders are unpaid, warns about fraud cases, and advises doing research before donating.

segments.title: Short episode transition
segments.summary: Josh says it is a rare short episode and they transition to listener mail.

segments.title: Tour thanks and upcoming dates
segments.summary: Hosts thank venues and audiences from the recent tour in Denver, Seattle and San Francisco, and promote upcoming shows in Madison, Chicago, Akron and Canada, plus ticket info and contact email.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Standard closing credit noting the show is an iHeartRadio production and directing listeners to the app and podcast platforms.
